issues.title: docs(api): declare Project.runEval in the OpenAPI contract
issues.body:
## Summary

`components.schemas.Project` did not declare `runEval`. Because `requestBodies.Project` is an `allOf` that reuses that schema, `PUT /api/projects` (the `projects_save` MCP tool) had no documented field for the per-project SOP run-evaluation policy, even though the server accepts and persists it.

Changes (one file, 21 insertions):

- Add `runEval` to `components.schemas.Project`, referencing a new `RunEvalPolicy` schema.
- Add `RunEvalPolicy` (`enabled`, `version`, `threshold`, `dimensions`) and `RunEvalDimension` (`id`, `name`, `question`, `weight`), matching `domain.RunEvalPolicy` / `domain.RunEvalDimension` in `internal/domain/run_eval.go`.

POST, PUT and the `Project` response all reuse `schemas.Project`, so they pick the field up together.

## Verification

- `go test ./docs/api/... ./internal/mcpserver/...` — pass
- `python3 scripts/check-public.py` — pass
- `ToolInputSchema(projects_save)` now declares `runEval`; a payload carrying the full policy passes `ValidateToolInput`
- `go test ./internal/httpapi` cannot compile in this checkout because `web/embed.go` embeds `web/native-chat/`, which requires the chatbot bundle to be built first. This is a build prerequisite, unrelated to the contract change.

## Deployment note

The contract is embedded into the binaries with `go:embed`, so running servers and MCP processes expose the updated schema only after a rebuild/restart.

issues.title: feat(web): share the chat composer's CLI/model picker across entries (#441)
issues.body:
Closes #441.

## What changed

Picking a CLI or model worked differently depending on where you were (#441). The chat composer (`chatbot/src/ModelPicker.jsx`) had search, brand logos, a "family · credits" line and a fixed check mark. The role wizard and 新建需求 in the classic SPA used plain inline menus with no search. Whenever a model's catalog family was `other`, they showed a gray "AI" badge, so "GPT-6.1 Sol" lost its GPT logo. The role wizard's CLI was also a plain dropdown.

This PR adds `AgentFlowAssistantModels.bindPicker` in `web/app/assistant-models.js`. It is the classic-SPA twin of `ModelPicker` and follows design.md's model-menu spec:

- It opens a menu attached to `<body>`, so dialogs and scrolling bodies no longer clip it. The menu is 240px wide, or the trigger's width up to 360px, with a 12px radius, at most 420px tall, and 6px from the trigger.
- It has search over name, id and family, brand icons, the "family · credits" line, a fixed check slot and an empty-result message.
- Keyboard: ArrowUp/ArrowDown, Home and End move through options, and Enter in the search box picks the first match. Escape closes only the menu, not the surrounding dialog, and returns focus to the trigger. Tab resumes the form's tab order from the trigger.
- It is mutually exclusive with `HuiPopover`, so only one popover is open at a time. It respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Brand inference now matches `modelProviderFor`: family first, then id, then name. Unknown brands show the Harness `brain` glyph instead of a lettered badge, and each CLI gets its logo, as `engineBrand` does in the chat.

Entries moved onto it:

- **角色定义**: CLI, model and 思考强度. The CLI keeps a hidden `select[name="executorId"]` (`data-native`) for its value, the legacy-executor option and the `change` event, so form handling and saving are unchanged.
- **新建需求 and the 澄清 tab**: the clarification model picker. It still lists CodeBuddy models only (#228).

Inline-menu CSS that no longer applies was removed, and `design.md` documents the shared picker.

Not in this PR:
- The 4th screenshot in the issue ("默认 Agent CLI") does not exist anywhere in this repository or its history, so it could not be changed here.
- Schedules, Bots, run evals and the SOP assistant still use their inline menus; design.md notes they move to `bindPicker` later. They already pick up the new brand inference and the chevron caret.

## Scope

- [x] Platform core / API / runner
- [ ] Public adapter / deployment
- [ ] Classic
- [ ] Portable
- [ ] Shared behavior contract
- [ ] Installer / CLI
- [ ] Documentation only

## Compatibility

Frontend only (`web/` and `design.md`). There are no API, database or migration changes. Saved role settings and the stored clarification model (`agentflow.clarifyModel`) are read and written exactly as before.

## Validation

```text
npm --prefix chatbot run build                        # needed so web/ can embed native-chat
go test ./web -count=1                                # ok
node web/assistant_models_test.js <bundle> web/app/assistant-models.js   # assistant models ok
npm --prefix webtest test                             # 189 passed
go vet ./web                                          # ok
python3 scripts/check-public.py                       # passed
bash scripts/scan-secrets.sh                          # no leaks found
```

`web/assistant_models_test.js` was rewritten on `web/hui_fake_dom.js` and covers the following:
- **Clarification picker**: search by name, id and family; the empty result; arrow keys; Escape not reaching the dialog; Enter picking the first match; outside press closing the menu.
- **Role wizard**: tested against the real `index.html` markup. Picking a CLI fires `change` once and the model and effort lists follow it. Only one menu is open at a time. The manual model-id field appears when chosen. Disabled triggers stay shut.

Browser check: Chromium via Playwright, with `/api` stubbed, opening the role wizard and 新建需求. I checked light and dark themes, a 1280px and a 420px viewport, the keyboard CLI switch, and Escape keeping the dialog open. This caught a dark-theme bug, now fixed: `product-v3.css`'s generic `input` rule had been painting a filled box inside the menu's search field.

Not run: the full `go test ./...`, the `local/` scripts, the e2e suite, and `npm --prefix chatbot test`. `chatbot/` is unchanged.

## Safety

- [x] I did not include credentials, internal endpoints, production data, or organization-specific infrastructure.
- [x] I preserved user files and unrelated changes.
- [ ] I updated generated Classic host bundles when applicable. (Not applicable.)
- [x] I documented third-party content and licensing changes when applicable. (No new third-party content. The brand patterns are ported from the existing `ModelProviderIcon.jsx`, and the logos are the ones already under `web/images/credentials`.)

issues.title: fix(runtime): reject checkpoints with borrowed Git object stores
issues.body:
## What changed

A workspace cloned with `git clone --shared` can have a regular `.git` directory while borrowing its Git objects through `.git/objects/info/alternates`. The checkpoint previously archived that pointer without its object store. After the source disappeared, the restored checkout could no longer read its history even though checkpoint capture had succeeded.

Capture now rejects nonempty or symlink alternate-store metadata, identifies the relative metadata path, and asks the operator to materialize borrowed objects in a standalone checkout before retrying. Empty regular alternates files remain accepted. The existing linked-worktree rejection also gains an actionable hint. Neither diagnostic resolves or prints the referenced target, and capture does not modify the source.

Synthetic tests cover root/nested metadata, relative pointers, empty alternates, unrelated files, symlinks, source preservation, and a real shared clone followed by an independent repack/checkpoint/restore. This complements the existing staged/unstaged and ignored/untracked preservation test rather than duplicating it.

## Scope

- [x] Platform core / API / runner
- [ ] Public adapter / deployment
- [ ] Classic
- [ ] Portable
- [ ] Shared behavior contract
- [ ] Installer / CLI
- [ ] Documentation only

This is a small checkpoint portability guard, separate from node checkpoint/rewind work in #413. It does not implement cross-machine handoff or ownership transfer.

## Compatibility

No schema or Runner protocol changes. Local and Runner captures using the shared runtime receive the same error. Previously accepted nonempty alternate-store metadata is intentionally rejected; existing checkpoint restoration remains unchanged. Capture failures retain the existing workspace preservation/reclamation safeguards. Default exclusions and isolation remain unchanged.

## Validation

Base: `Tencent/LoopForge` main at `dd56585276d8ecb6e0d6865f55e255194d75f85a`.

Passed locally:
- `python3 scripts/check-public.py`
- `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check`
- A separate synthetic Git reproduction: archiving a shared clone and removing its source makes `git show HEAD:tracked.txt` fail; after repacking borrowed objects and removing the alternate in the synthetic clone, history remains readable and `git fsck --full` succeeds. This reproduces the underlying Git dependency; it is **not** execution of the Go tests.

Blocked locally:
- `go test ./internal/runtime -run 'TestWorkspaceCheckpoint(GitMetadataDiagnostics|RejectsSymlinkAlternateStore|SharedCloneRequiresIndependentObjects)$' -count=1 -timeout=180s` — shell returned `go: command not found`. No toolchain was installed.

Not run: Go formatting/compiler validation, full Go suite, `go vet`, chatbot build/tests, browser acceptance, or `scripts/scan-secrets.sh` (downloads a Linux-only scanner). The PR remains draft pending Go/CI validation and review.

## Safety

- [x] I did not include credentials, internal endpoints, production data, or organization-specific infrastructure.
- [x] I preserved user files and unrelated changes.
- [x] Generated Classic host bundles are not applicable; none changed.
- [x] No third-party code/assets or dependencies were added.

Prepared with Codex assistance.
